newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra to review legality of savings charge.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra to review legality of savings charge.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday the government would review the legality of the surcharge imposed on the retirement savings of higher income earners to raise A$500 million a year.
But the government's advisers had already considered and rejected the constitutional doubts that leading lawyer Dennis Rose expressed on Tuesday, he said.
"We'll take Dennis Rose's opinion and we'll go off to our own lawyers and we'll say to them 'does this change anything that, any view that you've taken?'," Costello said on radio.
One of the many savings announced in Costello's August budget was a rise in the concessional tax rate on superannuation contributions for people earning more than A$70,000 a year.
The current rate is only 15 percent -- well below the 48 percent top income-tax rate -- and the government, calling this an obvious opportunity for tax avoidance, wants to raise it to 30 percent .
But the measure is being imposed as a charge on the superannuation funds, not as a tax on the income-earner.

Rose, formerly the government's own chief lawyer, said on Tuesday that the measure therefore contravened the constitution's requirement that the Federal government take people's property only on just terms, a provision that does not affect tax.
The Labor opposition on Wednesday called for the government to release its legal opinion showing that the charge was constitutional.
The legislation giving effect to the charge has not yet passed through parliament and could still be easily amended, as it might be if the government needed to bring it within the constitution.
The charge has applied since budget night, August 20, but the revenue will not flow to the government until the fiscal year that begins in July 1997.
